accepts.description: Backtest an algorithmic trading strategy. Submit strategy source code (written in the TypeScript/PineScript-style DSL described by the companion strategy codegen prompt endpoint); the service statically checks it against real historical market data, then returns quantitative performance metrics — net return, Sharpe / Sortino / Calmar, max drawdown, win rate, profit factor, plus the full trade list and equity curve. Use it to create, iterate on and quantitatively evaluate trading strategies, tune parameters, and A/B compare variants. Supports crypto perpetual pairs (e.g. BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT) and US-stock pairs (e.g. AAPL-USD, GOLD-USDC).

code.description: Full strategy source code to validate and backtest, written in the trading DSL. Call the companion strategy-codegen-prompt endpoint first if you need the language rules and API reference to generate it.

symbol.description: Trading pair to backtest. Crypto perps (BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT) and US-stock pairs (AAPL-USD, GOLD-USDC) are supported. Default BTCUSDT. Unknown symbols fail the request.

endTime.description: Window end date, format YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today when omitted.

slippage.description: Per-fill slippage as a decimal fraction of price (0.0005 = 0.05%). Default 0 (disabled).

startTime.description: Window start date, format YYYY-MM-DD. Optional — auto-derived from the interval when omitted. Ranges over the 200,000-bar cap are rejected.

makerFeeRate.description: Maker fee rate as a decimal fraction (0.0002 = 0.02%). Default 0 (frictionless).

takerFeeRate.description: Taker fee rate as a decimal fraction (0.0005 = 0.05%). Default 0 (frictionless). Set this (with makerFeeRate / slippage) for a deployability-realistic backtest.

initialBalance.description: Starting capital in USD. Defaults to the strategy code’s declaration, otherwise 10000.

valid.description: Present and false ONLY on static-validation failure; absent on a successful run.

trades.description: Round-trip trade records (one row per entry→exit), for inspecting individual fills.

totalFees.description: Total fees paid (USD) given the fee inputs.

equityCurve.description: Equity curve as [{ time, value }] points for plotting cumulative performance.

netPnlPercent.description: Net return as a percent of initial balance.

buyHoldReturnPercent.description: Buy & hold return over the same window, percent.

strategyOutperformance.description: Strategy return minus buy & hold, percent.

output.description: On validation failure: { valid: false, errors: string[], warnings: string[] }. example.label: paid-demo:risky-container-build
example.summary: BLOCK: 12 finding(s) across 1 build stage(s); 9 require resolution or explicit approval.

limitations: Does not inspect image layers, package vulnerabilities, signatures, provenance, or runtime configuration.
Cannot verify .dockerignore contents or whether a remote artifact checksum is correct.
Findings are static release gates and do not replace an image scan or sandboxed build.

findings.message: The final stage does not establish a non-root runtime user.
findings.remediation: Create or select a non-root account and set USER in the final stage.

findings.message: The base image is untagged or uses the mutable latest tag.
findings.remediation: Use a trusted image version and pin its sha256 digest.

findings.message: ARG declares 1 secret-like key(s); values are intentionally omitted.
findings.remediation: Pass build credentials with BuildKit secret or SSH mounts instead of ARG or ENV.

findings.message: ENV declares 1 secret-like key(s); values are intentionally omitted.
findings.remediation: Pass build credentials with BuildKit secret or SSH mounts instead of ARG or ENV.

findings.message: ADD downloads a remote resource without an explicit checksum.
findings.remediation: Use ADD --checksum=sha256:<digest>, or download and verify the artifact in one RUN layer.

findings.message: A secret-like credential or configuration path is copied into an image layer; the path value is omitted.
findings.remediation: Exclude the file with .dockerignore and inject required credentials through runtime or BuildKit secrets.

findings.message: A remotely downloaded script is piped directly to a shell.
findings.remediation: Download a versioned artifact, verify its checksum or signature, inspect it, then execute it.

findings.message: A download command disables TLS certificate verification.
findings.remediation: Restore certificate verification and trust only an explicit CA when required.

findings.message: RUN creates world-writable permissions with chmod 777.
findings.remediation: Grant the narrowest owner/group permissions required by the runtime user.

findings.message: The production final stage has no active HEALTHCHECK instruction.
findings.remediation: Add a bounded HEALTHCHECK or document that the orchestrator owns equivalent probes.

findings.message: WORKDIR uses a relative path.
findings.remediation: Use an absolute WORKDIR for predictable filesystem layout.

findings.message: CMD uses shell form, which can complicate signal and argument handling.
findings.remediation: Use JSON exec form for CMD when shell expansion is not required.

approval_gates: Resolve or explicitly approve 9 critical/high finding(s) before publishing the image.
Confirm that no credential remains in image layers, build history, or copied context.
Require a documented exception if the production process must run as root.

example.label: paid-demo:insecure-admin-contract
example.summary: BLOCK: 8 finding(s) across 2 operation(s); 5 high, 2 medium, 1 low.

rules: resource bounds for pagination and request bodies
sensitive response and privileged input fields
deployment transport and API inventory hygiene
coverage.limitations: A contract cannot prove runtime authorization, rate limiting, input enforcement, or exploitability; verify findings against implementation and gateway policy.

findings.summary: An API key is transmitted in the URL query string.
findings.remediation: Move credentials to an Authorization or purpose-specific request header.

findings.summary: An unauthenticated success response documents sensitive-looking fields.
findings.remediation: Require object/property authorization and remove secrets from response schemas.
findings.owasp_api_2023: API3:2023 Broken Object Property Level Authorization

findings.summary: A state-changing operation does not require documented authentication.
findings.remediation: Require an appropriate security scheme and enforce function-level authorization.

example.summary: 2 Kubernetes object(s), 1 workload(s), and 1 container(s) produced 18 finding(s): 2 critical, 12 high, 2 medium, 2 low.

findings.message: ClusterRole grants wildcard RBAC permissions.
findings.remediation: Replace wildcard verbs, resources, and URLs with the minimum required set.

findings.message: Container api disables normal container isolation.
findings.remediation: Set privileged to false and grant only the specific capability required.

findings.message: Container api embeds a secret-like environment variable as a literal value.
findings.remediation: Use valueFrom.secretKeyRef or an external secret provider.

findings.message: Container api does not explicitly disable privilege escalation.
findings.remediation: Set securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation to false.

findings.message: Container api adds capabilities outside the baseline allowlist.
findings.remediation: Remove added capabilities and grant only an explicitly allowed capability.

findings.message: Container api adds a capability forbidden by the Restricted profile.
findings.remediation: Remove the capability; Restricted permits only NET_BIND_SERVICE.

findings.message: Container api does not drop all Linux capabilities.
findings.remediation: Set capabilities.drop to [ALL], then add back only NET_BIND_SERVICE if needed.

findings.message: Container api is not required to run as a non-root user.
findings.remediation: Set runAsNonRoot: true at the Pod or container level.

findings.message: Container api explicitly runs as UID 0.
findings.remediation: Use a non-zero UID and set runAsNonRoot: true.

findings.message: Container api lacks a Restricted-compatible seccomp profile.
findings.remediation: Set seccompProfile.type to RuntimeDefault or an approved Localhost profile.

findings.message: Container api explicitly disables seccomp confinement.
findings.remediation: Use RuntimeDefault or an approved Localhost seccomp profile.

findings.message: Pod shares the host Network namespace.
findings.remediation: Remove hostNetwork: true unless this workload is explicitly isolated and approved.

findings.message: Volume type is outside the Restricted Pod Security allowlist.
findings.remediation: Use configMap, CSI, downwardAPI, emptyDir, ephemeral, PVC, projected, or secret.

findings.message: Pod mounts a path from the host filesystem.
findings.remediation: Replace hostPath with an allowed volume type or isolate the workload.

findings.message: Container api uses an unpinned or latest image reference.
findings.remediation: Pin the image by digest or an immutable release tag.

findings.message: Container api lacks complete CPU and memory requests or limits.
findings.remediation: Set CPU and memory requests and limits appropriate for the workload.

findings.message: Pod does not explicitly disable automatic service-account token mounting.
findings.remediation: Set automountServiceAccountToken: false when Kubernetes API access is unnecessary.

findings.message: Container api does not require a read-only root filesystem.
findings.remediation: Set readOnlyRootFilesystem: true and mount writable paths explicitly.

approval_gates: Remove added capabilities and grant only an explicitly allowed capability.
Remove hostNetwork: true unless this workload is explicitly isolated and approved.
Remove the capability; Restricted permits only NET_BIND_SERVICE.
Replace hostPath with an allowed volume type or isolate the workload.
Replace wildcard verbs, resources, and URLs with the minimum required set.
Set capabilities.drop to [ALL], then add back only NET_BIND_SERVICE if needed.
Set privileged to false and grant only the specific capability required.
Set runAsNonRoot: true at the Pod or container level.
Set seccompProfile.type to RuntimeDefault or an approved Localhost profile.
Set securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation to false.
Use RuntimeDefault or an approved Localhost seccomp profile.
Use a non-zero UID and set runAsNonRoot: true.

example.summary: BLOCK: 16 finding(s) across 1 service(s); 10 require resolution or explicit approval.

limitations: Accepts the caller's already parsed Compose JSON and does not resolve interpolation, profiles, includes, extends, anchors, or environment files.
Does not inspect image metadata, layers, vulnerabilities, signatures, provenance, or Dockerfile contents.
Does not verify host firewall rules, runtime defaults, secret-manager policy, external resource ownership, or the effective deployed model.
Static findings do not replace docker compose config validation, image scanning, runtime policy, or a sandboxed deployment test.

findings.message: The service adds all Linux capabilities.
findings.remediation: Drop all capabilities and add back only the minimum required set.

findings.message: The service assigns 1 secret-like environment value(s); values are intentionally omitted.
findings.remediation: Use Compose secrets or an external secret manager and rotate any exposed value.

findings.message: The service requests a privileged container with near-host-level runtime access.
findings.remediation: Remove privileged mode and grant only the exact devices and capabilities required.

findings.message: A container runtime socket is mounted into the service, enabling control of the host daemon.
findings.remediation: Remove the socket; use a narrowly scoped authenticated API or a rootless proxy if unavoidable.

findings.message: The runtime image is untagged or uses the mutable latest tag.
findings.remediation: Pin a trusted image by sha256 digest and automate reviewed digest updates.

findings.message: The service joins the host network namespace.
findings.remediation: Use an isolated container namespace and expose only the required interface.

findings.message: The service joins the host PID namespace.
findings.remediation: Use an isolated container namespace and expose only the required interface.

findings.message: A sensitive service port is published on all host interfaces.
findings.remediation: Bind to an explicit trusted interface or place the service behind an authenticated proxy and firewall.

findings.message: The service disables Docker's default seccomp confinement.
findings.remediation: Use the default seccomp profile or a narrower reviewed profile.

findings.message: The service explicitly runs as root.
findings.remediation: Select a numeric non-root UID/GID and keep required files owned by that account.

findings.message: The production service has no visible CPU, memory, or process limit.
findings.remediation: Set bounded CPU, memory, and PID limits supported by the target Compose runtime.

findings.message: The service disables the kernel OOM killer and can threaten host availability.
findings.remediation: Keep OOM killing enabled and enforce an explicit memory limit.

findings.message: The container root filesystem is not explicitly read-only.
findings.remediation: Set read_only: true and mount bounded writable tmpfs or volumes where required.

findings.message: The service does not explicitly prevent acquisition of new privileges.
findings.remediation: Add security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true].

findings.message: The service does not explicitly drop all default Linux capabilities.
findings.remediation: Set cap_drop: [ALL] and add back only capabilities proven necessary.

findings.message: The production service has no active Compose healthcheck.
findings.remediation: Add a bounded healthcheck or document an equivalent external probe.

approval_gates: Resolve or explicitly approve 10 critical/high finding(s) before starting the Compose project.
Confirm that no credential remains in Compose, environment files, process arguments, image history, or logs.
Require a documented owner and expiration date for every host-access exception.
Verify firewall, authentication, and intended interface binding for every published port.

body.doc: Alice from acme@example.com filed a support ticket on 2026-06-21 about the checkout flow returning a 502 from api.acme.com/v2/orders. Engineer Bob investigated and found the issue was a connection-pool exhaustion in the order-service: postgres max_connections was 100 and the pool had been silently leaking since the rollout of feature flag #orders-2026. Fix landed in commit 9a3b2c1; deploy went out 2026-06-22. Follow-up: add pgbouncer in front of the order-service and an alert on pool.in_use / max_connections > 0.8 in PagerDuty. Slack thread: #incident-orders-502. Mentioned engineers: @alice @bob @carol.

extra.serviceDescription: x402Factory Solana→Base USDC microbridge for agents. Deposits USDC on Solana and delivers USDC on Base with a small commission.

accepts.description: Solana → Base USDC microbridge. This request will accept a payment of 50.000000 USDC on Solana to the bridge wallet and, after a 2.5% commission of approximately 1.250000 USDC, will attempt to deliver around 48.750000 USDC on Base to the specified receiver. If the Base transfer cannot be completed after 2 attempts, the bridge refunds the full original amount on Solana; if the refund also fails after 3 attempts, the bridge is marked as failed and manual support is required.

amount.description: Amount in USDC to bridge from Solana to Base. Optional; minimum 0.01 USDC, maximum 50.00 USDC, steps of 0.01 USDC. When omitted, defaults to 1.00 USDC.

receiver.description: Destination Base wallet address (0x...) that should receive bridged USDC.

ok.description: True when the bridge completed (sent or refunded).

action.description: Action performed, always 'bridge_usdc_solana_to_base'.

status.description: Bridge status: 'sent' when Base transfer succeeded, 'refunded' when Solana refund was sent, or 'failed' when both send and refund failed.

base_txid.description: Base transaction hash of the USDC transfer to the receiver.

bridge_id.description: Internal bridge id for support and debugging.

accepts.description: Solana GPT wrapper API using x402 payments. Default direct call: model gpt-5-mini, max_output_tokens=2000, fixed price 0.01 USDC for up to 1000 input tokens. For all other settings the price is computed per model as (input_tokens * input_price_per_million + max_output_tokens * output_price_per_million) / 1,000,000, with a minimum of 0.001 USDC and always rounded up to 6 decimals. Optional max_input_tokens lets you cap the input tokens used for pricing; if the message is longer than this cap the server returns an error instead of under-pricing. Optional action=message (or omitting action) performs a direct GPT call with the given message. Optional action=create creates a custom agent with the given message as preprompt for 0.001 USDC (no OpenAI call), stores a base_price_usdc using (max_input_tokens_for_agent or 1000) + preprompt + max_output_tokens, and returns a custom_id. Optional action=list lists up to 100 recent custom agents for the paying wallet for 0.001 USDC without calling OpenAI. Custom agents can be called via POST /solana/llm/gpt with custom_id, or POST /solana/llm/gpt/{custom_id}. Each custom agent has a fixed price per call based on its stored preprompt, model, max_output_tokens and max_input_tokens; if the runtime message is longer than max_input_tokens the server returns an error. This specific request uses model gpt-5-mini with max_output_tokens=2000. Pricing mode: default. Prepaid price (x402) for this request: 0.010000 USDC. Estimated input tokens for pricing: 41.

num.description: The maximum number of records to return.

pair.description: The contract address (Uniswap V2/V3) or pool ID (Uniswap V4) of the liquidity pool to fetch trades for. When present, overrides token_address and paired_token_address.

side.description: Specifies trade side for the given token_address.

order.description: Sort order: asc (oldest first) or desc (newest first).

max_usd.description: Maximum trade size in USD. Filters out trades with an estimated USD value above this threshold. Calculated using on-chain price data at the time of the trade. Note: Adds additional SLAM cost to the query. A maximum of 10,000 trades that would otherwise match this query will be scanned.

min_usd.description: Minimum trade size in USD. Filters out trades with an estimated USD value below this threshold. Calculated using on-chain price data at the time of the trade. Note: Adds additional SLAM cost to the query. A maximum of 10,000 trades that would otherwise match this query will be scanned.

start_block.description: Block number to start the search from (inclusive). Defaults to the latest block in desc order, or the genesis block in asc order.

wallet_role.description: Filter trades where the specified wallet_address acted in the given role. Trader (default) where the wallet sent or received the token, regardless of initiating the swap transaction, or maker where the wallet initiated the swap transaction.

estimate_cost.description: When true returns the SLAM token cost for this query. It does not return any data or incur any actual charges.

token_address.description: The ERC-20 token contract address to fetch trades for.

wallet_address.description: The wallet address to fetch trades for.

start_log_index.description: Log index within the starting block to resume pagination or refine the starting point.

start_timestamp.description: Start searching from this UTC timestamp (inclusive). If provided, overrides start_block as the starting point.

paired_token_address.description: Filter trades where the specified token was swapped against this paired token address, regardless of pool.

slam.description: The SLAM token cost for this API call.

chain.description: The name of the blockchain network (e.g., base).

accepts.description: Solana GPT wrapper API using x402 payments. Default direct call: model gpt-5-mini, max_output_tokens=2000, fixed price 0.01 USDC for up to 1000 input tokens. For all other settings the price is computed per model as (input_tokens * input_price_per_million + max_output_tokens * output_price_per_million) / 1,000,000, with a minimum of 0.001 USDC and always rounded up to 6 decimals. Optional max_input_tokens lets you cap the input tokens used for pricing; if the message is longer than this cap the server returns an error instead of under-pricing. Optional action=message (or omitting action) performs a direct GPT call with the given message. Optional action=create creates a custom agent with the given message as preprompt for 0.001 USDC (no OpenAI call), stores a base_price_usdc using (max_input_tokens_for_agent or 1000) + preprompt + max_output_tokens, and returns a custom_id. Optional action=list lists up to 100 recent custom agents for the paying wallet for 0.001 USDC without calling OpenAI. Custom agents can be called via POST /solana/llm/gpt with custom_id, or POST /solana/llm/gpt/{custom_id}. Each custom agent has a fixed price per call based on its stored preprompt, model, max_output_tokens and max_input_tokens; if the runtime message is longer than max_input_tokens the server returns an error. Custom LLM agent AW5793DBAYAHSEHJTU on Solana. Model gpt-5-mini, max_input_tokens=5000, max_output_tokens=5300. Preprompt preview (first 150 chars): "Here is a prompt i received from a client, we going to forward it to next step but you need to add the info "create a rap" in before of the prompt, yo". Pricing mode: agent-per-token. Prepaid price (x402) for this request: 0.017932 USDC. Estimated input tokens for pricing: 5079.

accepts.description: Solana GPT wrapper API using x402 payments. Default direct call: model gpt-5-mini, max_output_tokens=2000, fixed price 0.01 USDC for up to 1000 input tokens. For all other settings the price is computed per model as (input_tokens * input_price_per_million + max_output_tokens * output_price_per_million) / 1,000,000, with a minimum of 0.001 USDC and always rounded up to 6 decimals. Optional max_input_tokens lets you cap the input tokens used for pricing; if the message is longer than this cap the server returns an error instead of under-pricing. Optional action=message (or omitting action) performs a direct GPT call with the given message. Optional action=create creates a custom agent with the given message as preprompt for 0.001 USDC (no OpenAI call), stores a base_price_usdc using (max_input_tokens_for_agent or 1000) + preprompt + max_output_tokens, and returns a custom_id. Optional action=list lists up to 100 recent custom agents for the paying wallet for 0.001 USDC without calling OpenAI. Custom agents can be called via POST /solana/llm/gpt with custom_id, or POST /solana/llm/gpt/{custom_id}. Each custom agent has a fixed price per call based on its stored preprompt, model, max_output_tokens and max_input_tokens; if the runtime message is longer than max_input_tokens the server returns an error. Preprompt preview (first 150 chars): "You are given a URL that points to an X (Twitter) profile image (PFP).  Your task: - Convert the image URL to a 400x400 version. - Do this by replacin". accepts.description: Create a Solana associated token account (ATA) for a given wallet and SPL mint so it can hold that token. Typical use: prepare a wallet to receive USDC or other SPL tokens before sending funds. Cost: $0.30 USDC. Without payment: checks via RPC whether the ATA already exists; if it does, returns 400 and no payment is needed. For paid calls, if the ATA cannot be created or is found to already exist at execution time, the server attempts to refund the full payment.

mint.description: Optional SPL token mint address for which to create the ATA. When omitted, the server uses its configured USDC_MINT for the current NETWORK.

target_wallet.description: Solana wallet address (base58) for which the associated token account (ATA) should be created.

ok.description: True when the ATA exists or was created after a paid call. False when the x402 payment had to be refunded.

mint.description: SPL mint used when checking/creating the ATA.

action.description: Action performed. For successful calls this is 'create_ata_dynamic'.

status.description: Operation status: 'created' when a new ATA was created, 'already_exists' when the ATA already existed, 'refunded' when the payment was refunded, or 'failed' when both ATA creation and refund failed.

message.description: Short human-readable summary of the outcome.

price_usdc.description: Price charged for this call in USDC (2 decimals, rounded up to $0.01).

ata_address.description: Associated token account address for the (wallet, mint) pair on Solana.

refund_txid.description: On-chain transaction signature for the refund when a paid call could not create the ATA or the ATA already existed at execution time.

payment_txid.description: On-chain transaction signature for the x402 payment that unlocked this endpoint, when available.

target_wallet.description: Wallet address for which the ATA was checked/created.

mint.description: SPL mint used when checking/creating the ATA.

action.description: Action performed. For successful calls this is 'create_ata_dynamic'.

status.description: Operation status: 'created' when a new ATA was created, 'already_exists' when the ATA already existed, 'refunded' when the payment was refunded, or 'failed' when both ATA creation and refund failed.

message.description: Short human-readable summary of the outcome.

price_usdc.description: Price charged for this call in USDC (2 decimals, rounded up to $0.01).

accepts.description: Solana text-to-speech API with fixed-price tiers paid via x402. Converts text input into a hosted audio URL. This endpoint is a fixed-price tier: '/solana/tts/100' charges exactly 1.000000 USDC prepaid. Within this tier, you can send up to 1666 characters (including spaces). If you send more, the server returns HTTP 400 and you should use a higher-priced /solana/tts/<amount> tier. Each integer segment after /solana/tts/ represents 0.01 USDC (e.g. /solana/tts/50 = 0.50 USDC, /solana/tts/1000 = 10.00 USDC).

accepts.description: Send messages to Telegram from your Solana wallet. Ideal for agents and backends to communicate with the outside world. Cost: 0.001 USDC per call. Use action=create with a name to get a chat_key, then open t.me/x402Factory_bot and send /pair <chat_key> to activate. Use action=list to see your chat_keys. Use action=message (or omit action) with chat_key and at least a message or attachment to send a Telegram message. Supports Markdown v2 and optional attachment URLs (image/video/audio).

name.description: Human-readable name to give to the Telegram bot/chat. Required for action=create. Ignored for other actions.

action.description: Optional action. Use 'create' to create a new chat_key, 'list' to list chat_keys for the paying wallet, or 'message' to explicitly send a message. When omitted, the call is treated as action=message and enqueues a message for an existing chat_key.

message.description: Message text in Markdown v2 format. When sending a message (action omitted or action=message), at least one of message or attachment is required. Not required for action=create or action=list.

chat_key.description: Chat key returned from action=create. Required when sending a message. Not used for action=create or action=list.

attachment.description: Optional URL of an attachment (image, video, or mp3) stored along with the message.

ok.description: True on success

name.description: Name associated with the chat_key (action=create or list).

chats.description: For action=list: up to 100 recent chats for the paying wallet, each with chat_key, name, chat_id, createdAt, updatedAt.

action.description: Action performed: 'create' for new chat_key, 'list' for listing chat_keys, 'message' when a message was enqueued.

chat_id.description: Telegram chat_id associated with the chat_key once the background worker has linked it. Initially empty.

chat_key.description: Chat key created for this wallet (action=create) or used for message sends.

createdAt.description: Creation timestamp for the chat or message.

updatedAt.description: Last update timestamp for the chat.

attachment.description: Attachment URL stored with the message, if any.

message_id.description: Identifier of the stored message row in the messages table.

tg_send_flag.description: Telegram send flag from the messages table. Initially empty; can be updated by a background worker.

activation_instructions.description: How to activate the Telegram bot for this chat_key (e.g. talk to t.me/x402Factory_bot and send /pair <chat_key>). Returned on create.

accepts.description: Send messages to Telegram from your Solana wallet. Ideal for agents and backends to communicate with the outside world. Cost: 0.001 USDC per call. Use action=create with a name to get a chat_key, then open t.me/x402Factory_bot and send /pair <chat_key> to activate. Use action=list to see your chat_keys. Use action=message (or omit action) with chat_key and at least a message or attachment to send a Telegram message. Supports Markdown v2 and optional attachment URLs (image/video/audio).

name.description: Human-readable name to give to the Telegram bot/chat. Required for action=create. Ignored for other actions.

action.description: Optional action. Use 'create' to create a new chat_key, 'list' to list chat_keys for the paying wallet, or 'message' to explicitly send a message. When omitted, the call is treated as action=message and enqueues a message for an existing chat_key.

message.description: Message text in Markdown v2 format. When sending a message (action omitted or action=message), at least one of message or attachment is required. Not required for action=create or action=list.

chat_key.description: Chat key returned from action=create. Required when sending a message. Not used for action=create or action=list.

attachment.description: Optional URL of an attachment (image, video, or mp3) stored along with the message.

ok.description: True on success

name.description: Name associated with the chat_key (action=create or list).

chats.description: For action=list: up to 100 recent chats for the paying wallet, each with chat_key, name, chat_id, createdAt, updatedAt.

action.description: Action performed: 'create' for new chat_key, 'list' for listing chat_keys, 'message' when a message was enqueued.

chat_id.description: Telegram chat_id associated with the chat_key once the background worker has linked it. Initially empty.

chat_key.description: Chat key created for this wallet (action=create) or used for message sends.

createdAt.description: Creation timestamp for the chat or message.

updatedAt.description: Last update timestamp for the chat.

attachment.description: Attachment URL stored with the message, if any.

message_id.description: Identifier of the stored message row in the messages table.

tg_send_flag.description: Telegram send flag from the messages table. Initially empty; can be updated by a background worker.

extra.serviceDescription: x402Factory Solana endpoints for agents (notes, LLMs, TTS, Telegram, coin prices, payments, X profiles).

accepts.description: Solana X profile mini-endpoint. Fetches a full X profile and the 10 most recent tweets for a given handle, returning the raw profile data plus a trimmed tweet list with key engagement metrics and media. Cost: 0.001 USDC per request.

handle.description: X handle (username) without the @ prefix, for example WURKDOTFUN or statikheadz.

ok.description: True on success.

handle.description: Normalized X handle that was requested.

tweets.description: Array of up to 10 recent tweets with trimmed but useful metadata: id, text, created_at, language, basic user info, engagement metrics, media and links.

profile.description: Full upstream X profile payload for the user, including core fields like id, rest_id, name, screen_name, description, avatar, location and counters.

price_usdc.description: Fixed price charged for this call in USDC (6 decimals).

tweet_count.description: Number of recent tweets returned (up to 10).
